To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a pharmacokinetic– pharmacodynamic model can be used to predict the tumour growth inhibition in xenograft mouse models after intermittent dosing with AZD8055.
AZD8055 inhibits mTORC1/2 and induces a dose‐dependent reduction in tumour size in a xenograft model of human cancer.

the pharmacodynamic effect of AZD8055 on tumour cell proliferation was best predicted by the area‐under‐the‐concentration curve (AUC) of inhibition of p70S6K phosphorylation, and that the duration of tumour growth inhibition was best predicted by a combination of the AUC and the maximum inhibition of p70 S6K phosphorylation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a mathematical model to predict tumour growth inhibition in response to AZD8055 in xenograft tumour models in vivo.
the development of a mathematical model of tumour growth and the application of this model to the design of optimal dose schedules.
the use of mathematical models to describe and predict the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of AZD8055, and to optimize the design of clinical trials with this compound.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model is useful for the purpose of predicting tumour growth in vivo after intermittent dosing, and for designing clinical studies.
the PK/PD model is useful for the rational design of the dose and schedule for AZD8055, which is a potent mTOR inhibitor with in vivo antitumor activity against a range a tumor types.
the model is useful for the prediction of the tumour growth inhibition for AZD8055 and could be used for the design of clinical trials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a pharmacokinetic– pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model that describes the effect of AZD8055 on tumour growth and that this can be used to optimize the dose schedule of AZD80551.

we have developed a pharmacokinetic– pharmacodynamic model that describes the time‐dependent effects of the mTOR inhibitor AZD8056 on the phosphorylation of the downstream target S6K1 and tumour growth inhibition.
the model is useful to describe the pharmacokinetic– pharmacodynamic data for the biomarkers, and to predict the antitumor effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the duration of mTOR inhibition is more important than the magnitude of the inhibition.
the PK/PD model can be used to optimize the dose, schedule, and duration of mTOR inhibitors.

a pharmacokinetic–biomarker–pharmacodynamic (PK–biomarker‐PD) model, incorporating both the maximum inhibition of mTORC1 and mTORC2 signalling and the duration of this inhibition, can be used to optimize the dosing regimen and to identify the optimal dose of a drug candidate.
